title: Policy-based NAT failover and service-ownership DNS handoff for controlplane egress
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customer private deployments running in constrained multi-AZ VPCs observed asymmetric egress after NAT failover and inconsistent DNS ownership when controlplane endpoints cross-account. This PR introduces a policy-driven NAT failover mechanism and a deterministic DNS handoff that ties service endpoints to an explicit ownership tag so that route propagation and resolver forwarding remain consistent during upgrades and AZ failover.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a controlplane egress policy layer (Terraform + Helm) that can pin egress traffic by service tag, prefer specified NAT gateways per-AZ, and fail over using prioritized policies instead of simple health-check rotation.
- Introduces a service_ownership tag on AWS endpoints and corresponding Route53 resolver conditional-forwarding entries to ensure DNS queries for controlplane subdomains resolve to the correct account/endpoint in cross-account setups.
- Adds idempotent reconcilers in the installer that detect mismatched endpoint tags and reconcile resolver rules without disrupting active sockets.
- Back-compat: existing clusters without the tag keep the current behavior; the installer can opt-in via `controlplane.egress.policy.enabled=true`.

Files and components affected (summary):
- terraform/modules/vpc/egress_policy.tf: new module that declares prioritized NAT groups and IAM to rotate ownership safely.
- helm/controlplane/templates/egress-policy-configmap.yaml: runtime config consumed by the controlplane agent.
- installer/hooks/reconcile_endpoint_tags.go: controller that ensures endpoint and resolver state converge.
- installer/upgrade/rollback.sh: quick rollback helper that re-applies prior resolver rules and drains affected instances.
- docs/operators/egress-and-dns.md: operator-facing docs describing parameters and troubleshooting.

Testing and validation steps performed:
- Unit tests for Terraform module logic + plan diffs for edge cases around multiple NATs (see commits).
- Integration test in staging VPC with a simulated cross-account endpoint and Route53 inbound/outbound rules verified.
- Blue/green upgrade in a dedicated test cluster to exercise the reconciler and rollback helper without request loss.

Upgrade notes / operator guidance:
- To enable: set `controlplane.egress.policy.enabled=true` and provide `controlplane.egress.policy.preferred_nats` list in values or Terraform var.
- For cross-account setups, ensure the installer principal has bless permissions to create or tag endpoints in the target account; see docs/operators/egress-and-dns.md for role assumption example.
- Rollback: run `installer/upgrade/rollback.sh <cluster>` which will re-apply previous resolver rules and fail back NAT weights safely.

Checklist: 
- [x] Terraform module + unit tests
- [x] Helm chart + helm lint
- [x] Installer reconciler implementation + e2e integration test
- [x] Docs and operator playbook
- [x] CI green and manual staging validation

Related: Linear ENG-3421 (egress policy workstream), INF-1188 (dns handoff design).

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids forcing a migration for existing clusters. The tag-based ownership allows a gradual rollout per-tenant. Follow-up PRs will add observability counters for failover events to the Redwood Console and an automated Linear task creator when resolver mismatches are observed.
